title: Advancements in Machine Learning for Customer Retention: A Systematic Literature Review of Predictive Models and Churn Analysis
venue: Journal of Sustainable Development and Policy
tldr: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 112 studies shows ensemble and deep learning models consistently outperform traditional classifiers for customer churn prediction across telecom, banking, e-commerce, and subscription services.
problem_and_motivation: Customer churn causes billions in annual revenue loss, yet organizations lack a consolidated understanding of which machine learning techniques perform best across industries. This gap hinders the adoption of accurate, interpretable, and ethically compliant predictive retention systems.
approach: Conducted a systematic literature review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines.
Searched 6 academic databases (Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar) using Boolean keyword combinations.
Screened 1,268 initial articles down to 116 empirical studies meeting inclusion criteria (2005–2025, peer-reviewed, ML applied to churn data with quantitative metrics).
Coded each study for algorithm type, dataset, evaluation metrics, sample size, industry domain, and publication year.
Standardized performance metrics (AUC-ROC, F1-score) and treated each model as a separate effect size entry.
Used R with 'metafor' package for fixed- and random-effects models, Hedges' g, heterogeneity (Q, I²), and subgroup analyses.
Assessed publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's test, and trim-and-fill procedure.
Conducted sensitivity analysis with leave-one-out diagnostics and influence plots.
findings: num: Ensemble models (gradient boosting, random forests) yielded the highest pooled AUC-ROC and F1-scores across datasets.
num: Deep learning models (RNNs, LSTMs, CNNs) excelled on time-series/behavioral data, reducing false-negative churn predictions by up to 30% relative to static models.
num: Feature engineering with RFM, lag variables, and temporal aggregations improved lift scores by 8–15 percentage points.
num: High-performing models consistently exhibited AUC-ROC above 0.80 and F1-scores above 0.70.
num: Imputation techniques improved lift scores by up to 15% compared to case-wise deletion.
num: CNN-based detectors reported up to ten-point AUC-ROC gains over gradient boosting when unstructured log data were available.
num: Deep Feature Synthesis (DFS) delivered lift gains of up to eight percentage points in SaaS churn competitions.
num: Incorporating network centrality measures in Graph Neural Networks improved churn AUC by capturing peer contagion effects.
num: SMOTE and cost-sensitive learning significantly improved recall in imbalanced datasets.
Public datasets (IBM Telco, Orange Telecom, UCI Bank) provided benchmarks with AUC-ROC spreads of 0.75–0.92 for state-of-the-art models.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides a comprehensive, evidence-based synthesis of machine learning techniques for customer churn prediction through a rigorous meta-analysis of 116 empirical studies. It establishes that ensemble methods (gradient boosting, random forests) and deep learning architectures (RNNs, LSTMs, CNNs) consistently outperform traditional statistical models, with quantified performance advantages across multiple industries. The study systematically maps the evolution of churn analytics from traditional regression to advanced representation learning, while identifying critical research gaps in model interpretability, privacy preservation, and cross-sectoral generalizability. By aggregating performance metrics and documenting the impact of feature engineering, data preprocessing, and evaluation frameworks, it offers a foundational reference that bridges academic methodology and practical deployment considerations. The paper also advances the field by highlighting emerging directions such as explainable AI, federated learning, and hybrid architectures, thus guiding future research toward more transparent, adaptable, and ethically compliant retention systems.
directly_justifies: Ensemble learning models consistently outperform traditional classifiers in churn prediction across diverse datasets.
Deep learning models excel in time-series and behavioral data, reducing false-negative churn predictions by up to 30%.
Feature engineering with RFM, lag variables, and temporal aggregations improves lift scores by 8–15 percentage points.
Model interpretability is a critical adoption factor; post-hoc tools like SHAP and LIME increase managerial trust.
Industry context significantly influences model selection—telecom favors ensembles, banking prioritizes interpretability, e-commerce adopts deep learning.
limits: Does not provide primary empirical data—findings are aggregated from secondary studies.
Focuses on general churn prediction; does not address culturally specific financial practices or Filipino-specific contexts.
Does not evaluate budget recommendation systems or allocation constraints directly.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains was performed. The paper directly addresses predictive modeling (6.A), classification approaches (5.C), and evaluation frameworks (12.A, 12.B) as its primary contributions. It provides strong supporting evidence for financial behavioral profiles (5.A), forecasting algorithms (6.B), and data privacy (10.A). Medium relevance was assigned to anomaly detection (8.A, 8.B), user trust (10.B), engagement dynamics (11.A), and synthetic data (14.A) because these are discussed but are not central. Profile dynamics (5.B) was rated medium due to coverage of concept drift. Budgeting topics (7.A, 7.B) were considered but rejected or rated low/contextual because the paper does not address budget allocation or recommendation. The paper has no relevance to Filipino young professionals (1.A–1.C), culturally specific practices (2.A–2.D), expense categorization (3.A–3.C), or mobile-first design (9.A–9.C), which were therefore excluded. The overall coverage is strongly centered on machine learning methodology and evaluation for churn prediction.

limitations: The review relies on published studies, which may overrepresent positive results due to publication bias. [unacknowledged]
Meta-analysis pooled results across heterogeneous datasets and evaluation protocols, potentially obscuring domain-specific nuances. [unacknowledged]
The paper does not address real-time deployment challenges or latency constraints of deep learning models. [unacknowledged]
Self-identified limitation: inconsistent reporting of model calibration across reviewed studies.
Self-identified limitation: limited availability of longitudinal datasets and underutilization of hybrid models in smaller firms.
